title: Rigveda 7.74: To Asvins
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.74: To Asvins: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.74 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Asvins. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 539v-540r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.74.1-3 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 5, varga 21); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 539v
translation.original_text:
1i̱mā u̍ vā̱ṁ divi̍ṣṭaya u̱srā ha̍vante aśvinā | a̱yaṁ vā̍m a̱hve 'va̍se śacīvasū̱ viśa̍ṁ-viśa̱ṁ hi gaccha̍thaḥ ||
2yu̱vaṁ ci̱traṁ da̍dathu̱r bhoja̍naṁ narā̱ code̍thāṁ sū̱nṛtā̍vate | a̱rvāg ratha̱ṁ sama̍nasā̱ ni ya̍cchata̱m piba̍taṁ so̱myam madhu̍ ||
3ā yā̍ta̱m upa̍ bhūṣata̱m madhva̍ḥ pibatam aśvinā | du̱gdham payo̍ vṛṣaṇā jenyāvasū̱ mā no̍ mardhiṣṭa̱m ā ga̍tam ||
translation.text:
1THESE morning sacrifices call you, Aṣvins, at the break of day. For help have I invoked you rich in power and might: for, house by house ye visit all.
2O Heroes, ye bestow wonderful nourishment. send it to him whose songs are sweet Accordant, both of you, drive your car down to us, and drink the savoury Soma juice.
3Approach ye and be near to us. drink, O ye Aṣvins, of the meath. Draw forth the milk, ye Mighty, rich in genuine wealth: injure us not, and come to us.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 539v (numbered 60v by the scribe) (OPenn image 540, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.73.2 ‹-yajate vandate ca aśnītam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 540r (numbered 61r by the scribe), begins in RV 7.74.4 ‹-dīyanti bibhrataḥ makṣuyu-bhiḥ narā›. Verses 7.74.1-3 end on this page.

1imāḥ | oṃ iti | vām | diviṣṭayaḥ | usrā | havante | aśvinā | ayam | vām | ahve | avase | śacīvasūitiśacī-vasū | viśam-viśam | hi | gacchathaḥ
2yuvam | citram | dadathuḥ | bhojanam | narā | codethām | sūnṛtāvate | arvāk | ratham | sa-manasā | ni | yacchatam | pibatam | somyam | madhu
3ā | yātam | upa | bhūṣatam | madhvaḥ | pibatam | aśvinā | dugdham | payaḥ | mā | naḥ | mardhiṣṭam | ā | gatam

translation.original_ref: RV 7.74.4-6 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 5, varga 21); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 540r
translation.original_text:
4aśvā̍so̱ ye vā̱m upa̍ dā̱śuṣo̍ gṛ̱haṁ yu̱vāṁ dīya̍nti̱ bibhra̍taḥ | ma̱kṣū̱yubhi̍r narā̱ haye̍bhir aśvi̱nā de̍vā yātam asma̱yū ||
5adhā̍ ha̱ yanto̍ a̱śvinā̱ pṛkṣa̍ḥ sacanta sū̱raya̍ḥ | tā ya̍ṁsato ma̱ghava̍dbhyo dhru̱vaṁ yaśa̍ś cha̱rdir a̱smabhya̱ṁ nāsa̍tyā ||
6pra ye ya̱yur a̍vṛ̱kāso̱ rathā̍ iva nṛpā̱tāro̱ janā̍nām | u̱ta svena̱ śava̍sā śūśuvu̱r nara̍ u̱ta kṣi̍yanti sukṣi̱tim ||
translation.text:
4The horses that convey you in their rapid flight down to the worshipper's abode, With these your speedy coursers, Heroes, Aṣvins, come, ye Gods, come well-inclined to us.
5Yea, verily, our princes seek the Aṣvins in pursuit of food. These shall give lasting glory to our liberal lords, and, both Nâsatyas, shelter us.
6Those who have led the way, like cars, offending none, those who are guardians of the men- Also through their own might the heroes have grown strong, and dwell in safe and happy homes.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 540r (numbered 61r by the scribe) (OPenn image 540, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.74.4 ‹-dīyanti bibhrataḥ makṣuyu-bhiḥ narā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 540v (numbered 61v by the scribe), begins in RV 7.75.4 ‹syā yujānā parākāt pañca›. Verses 7.74.4-6 end on this page; 7.74.4 begins on fol. 539v (numbered 60v by the scribe).
